'''David G. Willey''' (born 4 November 1947), known as the '''Mad Scientist''', is an English former [[physics]] instructor at the [[University of Pittsburgh at Johnstown]]<ref name="UPJ">{{cite web|url=http://www.upj.pitt.edu/|title=UPJ|website=upj.pitt.edu}}</ref> in [[Johnstown, Pennsylvania]]. He has been presenting physics shows since the early 1980s. Willey is a scientific consultant for the skeptics group [[Committee for Skeptical Inquiry]]  (C.S.I.).<ref name="C.S.I.">{{cite web|url=http://www.csicop.org/si/show/physics_behind_four_amazing_demonstrations|title=The Physics Behind Four Amazing Demonstrations|date=November 1999|publisher=csicop.org}}</ref> He also designs physics apparatus and equipment for the Science Kit Boreal Labs.<ref name="Science Kit">{{cite web |url=http://sciencekit.com/david-willey/a/362/ |title=David Willey - Science Kit |access-date=2012-04-10 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20110209074857/http://sciencekit.com/david-willey/a/362/ |archive-date=9 February 2011 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

==Education and career==
Willey studied at [[Aston University]] and [[Birmingham University]]<ref name="Birmingham University">{{cite web|url=http://www.birmingham.ac.uk/index.aspx|title=University of Birmingham|publisher=University of Birmingham}}</ref> from 1966 to 1971.  Then he taught at Saltley Grammar School,<ref name="Saltley School">{{cite web|url=http://www.saltley.bham.sch.uk/|title=Saltley Academy|website=saltley.bham.sch.uk|access-date=18 April 2012|archive-date=25 April 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120425081955/http://www.saltley.bham.sch.uk/|url-status=dead}}</ref> in Birmingham from 1971 to 1972.  Next, Willey moved from his home country of England to the United States and enrolled at the [[Ohio State University]].<ref name="OSU">{{cite web|url=http://www.osu.edu/|title=Home page|year= 2017|publisher= The Ohio State University}}</ref> He was in [[Columbus, Ohio]], until he obtained his master's degree in physics in 1974.  His first teaching position was with the University of Pittsburgh at Johnstown.  In the early 1980s, he performed his first physics show at the university's open house.

A few months later, Willey made a 15-minute video of physics demonstrations with a group of troubled boys from a remand home.  This video was played on local television for the public to see.  A local school teacher saw Willey's demonstrations and asked him to perform some of them for her class.  Willey then began a physics show called "How Does A Thing Like That Work?".<ref name="How Does A Thing Like That Work">{{cite web |url=http://www.dwilley.com/ |title=Home Page |accessdate=2012-04-10 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120316221022/http://dwilley.com/ |archivedate=16 March 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref>

Looking for the next big physics demonstrations, Willey found [[firewalking]]. He teamed up with the Norwegian physicist, Kjetil Kjernsmo<ref name="Kjetil Kjernsmo">{{cite web|url=http://www.kjetil.kjernsmo.net/cv|title=Kjetil Kjernsmo's Curriculum Vitae (CV) / Resume|website=kjetil.kjernsmo.net}}</ref> of [[University of Oslo]], to study the physics behind firewalking.  They developed a computer model of a foot while a person firewalked. They needed data from long walks and hot walks to verify the computer model. A firewalking group from [[Seattle, Washington|Seattle]] volunteered to perform the first walk. On 18 October 1997, in [[Redmond, Washington]], Michael McDermott walked across a bed of [[coals]] that were at a temperature of {{cvt|1813|°F}}.<ref name="Michael McDermott">{{Cite web |url=http://www.weirdwashington.us/the%20cut.htm |title=What |access-date=12 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120801021817/http://www.weirdwashington.us/the%20cut.htm |archive-date=1 August 2012 |url-status=dead }}</ref>  Willey also walked on that fire bed, but not at the record temperature.

Willey's next, and most famous firewalk, was in July 1998 at the University of Pittsburgh at Johnstown. This firewalk was {{convert|165|feet|0}} long to break the world record for the longest distance walking on fire.<ref name="Fire walk record">{{cite web|url=http://www.happinessquest.com/firewalk.html|title=Firewalk – History, Seminars, World Record Holder, Firewalking|publisher=happinessquest.com|access-date=11 April 2012|archive-date=30 August 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120830052353/http://www.happinessquest.com/firewalk.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> His walk was recorded and shown on television by the [[BBC]] and [[American Broadcasting Company|ABC]].  This got the attention of the producers of ''[[The Tonight Show with Jay Leno]]''.  Willey's nickname, "Mad Scientist", was born.  For the next 10 years (1998–2008) Willey performed physics demonstrations on ''The Tonight Show''.<ref name="IMDb 1998">{{cite web | title="The Tonight Show with Jay Leno" Matthew Perry/David Willey/Meat Loaf (TV Episode 1998) | website=IMDb | date=12 November 1998 | url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0728271/ | access-date=9 March 2022}}</ref><ref name="Getty Images 2003">{{cite web | title=Mad Scientist David Willey appears on "The Tonight Show with Jay... | website=Getty Images | date=10 October 2003 | url=https://www.gettyimages.com/detail/news-photo/mad-scientist-david-willey-appears-on-the-tonight-show-with-news-photo/2580377 | language=de | access-date=9 March 2022}}</ref>  He appeared on the show 19 times.  During this time, Willey also appeared on other television shows such as ''[[Time Warp (TV series)|Time Warp]]'',<ref name="Time Warp">{{cite web |url=http://www.yourdiscovery.com/video/shows/time-warp |title=Time Warp Videos at YourDiscovery.com |accessdate=2012-04-11 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20120415144128/http://www.yourdiscovery.com/video/shows/time-warp/ |archivedate=15 April 2012 |df=dmy-all }}</ref> ''Humanly Impossible'',{{citation needed|date=January 2016}} ''[[Talk Soup]]'',{{citation needed|date=January 2016}} ''[[Steve Harvey's Big Time]]'',<ref name="Steve Harvey's Big Time">{{cite web|url=http://www.thefutoncritic.com/news/2003/10/30/the-wb-maps-november-sweeps-plans-16237/6227/|title=Breaking News - The WB Maps November Sweeps Plans |publisher=thefutoncritic.com}}</ref> ''King 5 TV'',{{citation needed|date=January 2016}} ''[[Skeptical Inquirer]]'',<ref name="Skeptical Inquirer">{{cite web|url=http://www.csicop.org/specialarticles/show/physics_instructor_who_walks_on_fire//|title=The Physics Instructor Who Walks on Fire|date=25 October 2000|publisher=csicop.org}}</ref> ''Extreme Body Parts'',{{citation needed|date=January 2016}} [[John Stossel]]'s ''Power of Belief'',<ref name="Power of Belief">{{cite web|url=http://www.liberator.net/articles/StosselBelief2.html|title=John Stossel Examines the Power of Belief [Transcript]|publisher=liberator.net}}</ref> the ''Crook and Chase Show'',<ref name="Crook and Chase Show">{{Cite web |url=http://www.locatetv.com/tv/crook-and-chase/1506703/ |title=Crook & Chase - EPISODE: 848 &#124; LocateTV |access-date=11 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131113225515/http://www.locatetv.com/tv/crook-and-chase/1506703 |archive-date=13 November 2013 |url-status=dead }}</ref> ''Science Park'',{{citation needed|date=January 2016}} ''[[Jensen!]]'',<ref name="Jensen">{{YouTube|id=Oi8ORuPdwE4|title=David Willey on "Jensen" in Amsterdam, first appearance}}</ref> ''[[Johannes B. Kerner]]'',<ref name="Johannes B. Kerner">http://www.zdf.de/ZDFmediathek/beitrag/video/362422/Eine+Frage+des+Glaubens+-+JBK+vom+15.11.#/beitrag/video/362422/Eine-Frage-des-Glaubens---JBK-vom-15.11./{{Dead link|date=July 2019 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> ''[[The Brian Conley Show]]'',{{citation needed|date=January 2016}} ''Fantasia'',{{citation needed|date=January 2016}} ''[[Penn & Teller: Bullshit!]]'',<ref name="P&T">{{cite web | title="Penn & Teller: Bullshit!" Self-Helpless (TV Episode 2003) | website=IMDb | date=21 March 2003 | url=https://www.imdb.com/title/tt0771120/ | access-date=9 March 2022}}</ref> ''Wednesday Night at the Lab'',<ref name="Wednesday Night at the Lab">{{cite web|url=http://eventful.com/madison/events/wednesday-night-lab-/E0-001-008327641-0/|title=Wednesday Night at the Lab|website=Eventful}}</ref> part of the 25th ''[[Wonders of Physics]]'' in [[Madison, Wisconsin]],<ref name="Wonders of Physics">{{cite web|url=http://sprott.physics.wisc.edu/demobook/uwpress.htm|title=Physics Demonstrations|first=J. C.|last=Sprott|website=sprott.physics.wisc.edu}}</ref> and a seven part series on the [[Shaolin Monks]] for the [[Canadian Discovery Channel]].{{citation needed|date=January 2016}}
